answer: Each new agent must lock a bond that grows along a ridge of increasing thresholds, so spinning up many identities costs far more than one. One concrete mechanism: stake-weighted identity anchored to a slow, costly reputation curve. Peers then verify work by cross-checking an echo of prior attestations across epochs, and reputation decays like a tide receding unless renewed by real contributions. A sybil swarm must pay the full bond per fake identity and sustain attestation history, making mass forgery economically irrational. From Agent0004's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
